readme: target presets - read by buildAppData.py into appData/targets.json
made in the 2026-10-10 research round, one researcher per preset; every source is listed in data/sources.md
offsets: weekly effective sets added to the user's baseline (the week slider, default 12) per region, -12..10; the app uses the highest target among the active presets
cardio: weekly minutes in the 3-zone model (z1 below the first threshold, z2 between, z3 above the second); the builder turns them into the cardio lights of cardio.json
keyExercises: the exercises the research names for the preset - tagged in the picker while it is on

marathon.name: Marathon
marathon.summary: Tough calves, glutes and hips for the miles; light upper body; mostly easy running.

why.calves: soleus/calf carries several times bodyweight every stride; weak calves go with Achilles trouble
why.glutes: hip extension strength and durability over tens of thousands of strides
why.gluteMed: hip abductor weakness is linked to knee pain and IT band trouble in runners
why.hamstrings: brake the swinging leg and help extend the hip; common strain site when tired
why.neck: no running need; cut to nothing
why.lats: only light arm-drive and posture work
why.frontDelt: no running need, avoid extra weight
why.sideDelt: no running need, avoid extra weight
why.upperChest: no running need, extra mass is a cost
why.lowerChest: no running need, extra mass is a cost
why.biceps: no running need, extra mass is a cost
why.triceps: no running need, extra mass is a cost

sprint.name: Sprinting
sprint.summary: Hamstrings, glutes, calves, hip flexors for speed; light upper body; tiny cardio

why.hamstrings: most common sprint injury; Nordics (about 48 reps/week) plus hip-dominant lifts
why.glutes: hip extension drives acceleration; heavy squat, thrust and RDL work 2-3x/week
why.calves: plantarflexors carry stance force; Achilles and soleus strains are top time-loss injuries
why.hipFlexors: fast leg recovery at top speed; sprinters have large psoas; hip torque limits speed
why.adductors: groin strain risk at full speed; sprinters show bigger adductors
why.gluteMed: pelvis stability on each single-leg landing
why.tibialis: foot dorsiflexion before ground contact; shin load from high impacts
why.lowerAbs: pelvic control against heavy hip flexor pull at speed
why.neck: no gym demand in sprinting; maintenance only
why.sideDelt: arm drive is front-to-back; no need for lateral delt volume
why.biceps: small role in arm swing; gets some work from pulling anyway

basketball.name: Basketball
basketball.summary: Jump and cut legs, calves, hips and knees for injury cover; light arms and chest.

why.calves: Every jump and push-off runs through calf and Achilles; Achilles pain is a common NBA complaint
why.midQuad: Jump height and landing braking; patellofemoral pain costs the most games in the NBA
why.innerQuad: Knee control on landing and cutting, jumper's knee protection
why.outerQuad: Jump and deceleration strength, knee protection
why.gluteMed: Hip abduction control keeps the knee from collapsing inward on cuts and landings
why.glutes: Hip extension drives jumps and sprints, shares load off knees and lower back
why.adductors: Groin adductor pain is a top-3 NBA complaint (about 10% of cases); heavy side-to-side cutting
why.hamstrings: Sprint injury cover and knee stability; Nordic-type work roughly halves hamstring injuries
why.tibialis: Ankle sprain is the most common basketball injury; shin muscles help control the foot
why.rotatorCuff: Overhead shooting, rebounding and contact on the shoulder
why.biceps: Little role in basketball; get it from pulling work and keep minimal
why.lowerChest: Pushing is for contact only, not a main driver
why.upperChest: Pushing is for contact only, not a main driver
why.upperAbs: Anti-rotation and bracing matter more than crunching
why.neck: Not a collision sport, maintenance only

soccer.name: Football (soccer)
soccer.summary: Hamstring and groin armour, sprint legs and calves; upper body kept to maintenance

why.hamstrings: Top muscle injury in football and the sprint engine; Nordics and hinges cut strains by about 65%
why.adductors: Groin pain is the other big football injury; Copenhagen adduction cut groin problems about 41%
why.glutes: Sprint acceleration, kicking and hamstring load-sharing
why.gluteMed: Pelvis stability on the single-leg plant when cutting and kicking
why.calves: Sprint push-off and calf strain protection in repeated sprints
why.hipFlexors: Knee drive in sprinting and the swing leg of the kick
why.outerQuad: Kick power and deceleration; the only quad region that needs a bump
why.neck: Heading only; a few sets of isometrics are enough, no need to build it
why.upperTraps: Not a performance limiter in football; maintenance only
why.midTraps: Not a performance limiter in football; maintenance only
why.lowerTraps: Not a performance limiter in football; maintenance only
why.rhomboids: Not a performance limiter in football; maintenance only
why.lats: Little upper-body pulling demand outside goalkeepers
why.frontDelt: Upper body is maintenance; pressing does not carry to the pitch
why.sideDelt: Upper body is maintenance; no overhead demand
why.rearDelt: Upper body is maintenance, posture work covers it
why.rotatorCuff: No throwing or overhead load (except goalkeepers and throw-ins)
why.upperChest: No pushing demand; incidental work from other lifts is plenty
why.lowerChest: No pushing demand; incidental work from other lifts is plenty
why.biceps: Not trained for football; leftover from rows and pull-ups is enough
why.triceps: Not trained for football; leftover from pressing is enough
why.upperAbs: Trunk bracing comes from planks and carries, not crunches

swimming.name: Swimming
swimming.summary: Pulling lats, healthy shoulders (cuff, serratus, rear back), core; light legs and chest

why.lats: main pulling muscle in the underwater pull; pull-ups and rows carry over directly
why.rotatorCuff: external rotators are the swimmer's-shoulder protection; 40-91% of swimmers get shoulder trouble
why.lowerTraps: scapular control against the huge repeated overhead reach
why.midTraps: scapular retraction balances the front-heavy stroke
why.rhomboids: scapular retractors, part of every shoulder prevention programme
why.rearDelt: back-of-shoulder strength offsets the front-dominant stroke
why.serratus: active through the whole stroke; keeps the shoulder blade moving cleanly
why.triceps: finishes the pull and drives the push phase
why.upperAbs: trunk stiffness transfers force and holds the streamline
why.lowerAbs: holds hips up and the kick connected to the body
why.obliques: body roll and rotation every stroke, flip turns
why.lowerBack: streamline, starts and pushing off the wall
why.neck: no real demand and the head stays neutral; maintenance only
why.tibialis: ankles are plantar-flexed in the kick, shins barely load; maintenance only

cycling.name: Cycling
cycling.summary: Heavy legs and glutes for power and bone, steady back and core, light upper body.

why.glutes: big hip extensor in every pedal stroke; heavy hinges and squats also load the hips and spine bone
why.hipFlexors: the pedal stroke already works them hard and the seated position shortens them, so no extra gym sets
why.frontDelt: bars only need support and posture; maintenance only
why.sideDelt: no riding demand and no performance link, so a few sets for health
why.upperChest: pressing is maintenance only; the bars give light pushing already
why.lowerChest: no riding demand at all; a few pushing sets keep the body balanced
why.serratus: light stabiliser while leaning on the bars; push-ups cover it
why.biceps: arms are minor for riding; they get plenty of indirect work from rows and pull-downs
why.triceps: arms support the body on the bars and are covered by presses; a few sets are enough
why.tibialis: ankle front muscle works lightly in the pedal stroke and does not limit performance

climbing.name: Climbing
climbing.summary: Grip, lats and shoulder-blade control, with push work to protect elbows and shoulders.

why.midTraps: scapular control while hanging and pulling
why.lats: main pulling muscle on steep walls; pull strength separates elite from intermediate
why.rotatorCuff: shoulder injury cover for long overhead loading
why.serratus: found weak in climbers overhead; scapular stability
why.forearms: finger flexors drive grip; forearm lean mass tracks grip strength; extensors guard the elbow
why.lowerAbs: feet-up body tension on steep and roofed terrain
why.obliques: trunk stability when a hand lifts off
why.hipFlexors: high steps, drawing the feet up, compression
why.calves: small role; toeing on holds is mostly bodyweight

combat.name: Boxing / MMA
combat.summary: Neck, obliques, shoulder endurance, grip and hips for striking and grappling

why.neck: isometric neck strength is linked to lower concussion odds, and clinch/grappling load the neck constantly
why.upperTraps: carry and stabilise the head and neck; shrugs and carries cover it cheaply
why.lats: pulling in clinches, guard and wrestling; also decelerates punches
why.lowerBack: takedowns, sprawls, hip-hinge power and trunk bracing; low back is a common combat injury site
why.frontDelt: keeps the guard up and repeats punches for 3 to 5 minute rounds
why.rearDelt: slows the arm after a punch and balances the rounded boxing posture
why.rotatorCuff: shoulder cuff strains and impingement are the classic boxing and grappling shoulder problems
why.serratus: drives reach and protraction at the end of a straight punch
why.triceps: elbow extension of jab, cross and hooks
why.forearms: grip endurance under fatigue matters in judo, BJJ and wrestling; wrists also take punch shock
why.obliques: trunk rotation and anti-rotation carry punch power and clinch work
why.glutes: hip drive into punches, kicks, takedowns and sprawls
why.gluteMed: stance stability and pivoting on one leg
why.adductors: wide stances, guard, kicks and cutting steps; groin strain protection
why.hamstrings: hip extension in takedowns, pivots and kicking; strain protection
why.calves: constant bouncing on the balls of the feet and pivoting
why.biceps: gets plenty of pulling work from grappling and rows; little direct need
why.lowerChest: pressing is covered by punching itself; heavy chest work adds little
why.innerQuad: no distinct role beyond what squats and lunges already give
why.tibialis: no special demand in this sport

vTaper.name: V-taper
vTaper.summary: Wide lats and side delts, upper chest, tight waist, legs and the rest kept at maintenance.

why.lats: the main width builder; ~20 weekly sets is the upper-middle of the evidence-backed range
why.sideDelt: shoulder width; responds to high volume, light-moderate loads, twice or more per week
why.upperChest: fills the upper torso and balances the shoulder line; incline pressing hits it hardest
why.rearDelt: rounds out shoulder width and balances all the pressing; usually under-trained
why.frontDelt: already worked hard by every press, so direct work only adds bulk
why.obliques: keeps the waist narrow; weighted side work adds thickness exactly where you want less
why.neck: no V-taper benefit, a thicker neck narrows the shoulder to neck contrast
why.forearms: grip work from rows and pulldowns covers it
why.hipFlexors: no look benefit; sitting already keeps them short, so only token work
why.adductors: maintenance only; squats and lunges give indirect sets
why.gluteMed: maintenance only; squats and lunges give indirect sets
why.tibialis: no look benefit; a few sets for shin and knee health is plenty

mew2.name: mew2
mew2.summary: Mewtwo build: huge thighs and tail-base glutes, narrow chest, twig arms, slim waist

why.glutes: the thick tail base sits right on the glutes; 20 sets/week is in the high-growth range
why.gluteMed: wide hips and thigh mass; side glute fills out the upper thigh/hip line
why.outerQuad: the thighs are the biggest thing on the character; quads respond to 20+ sets/week
why.midQuad: the thighs are the biggest thing on the character; quads respond to 20+ sets/week
why.innerQuad: full thigh width front and inside needs the whole quad trained, teardrop included
why.adductors: adductor magnus is a big inner-thigh/hip extensor that squats and deep lunges grow
why.hamstrings: thick back of the thigh; hip-flexed leg curls grow them best (Maeo)
why.calves: thick lower leg to carry the big thighs; moderate extra on top of baseline
why.neck: long thin neck, so health-level work only
why.upperTraps: narrow sloped shoulders; no trap growth wanted
why.midTraps: narrow upper back; posture-level work only
why.rhomboids: narrow upper back; posture-level work only
why.frontDelt: narrow shoulders; presses and pushing already add front delt, so 3 sets is plenty
why.sideDelt: side delts are what make shoulders wide, which is the opposite of this look
why.rearDelt: kept at 6 sets to balance the shoulder joint without adding width
why.rotatorCuff: 6 sets of cuff work keeps shoulders healthy under heavy leg-day-biased training
why.upperChest: narrow chest; just enough pressing for a healthy push pattern
why.lowerChest: narrow chest; just enough pressing for a healthy push pattern
why.biceps: thin arms; 3 sets/week is a maintenance dose (pulling work adds more)
why.triceps: thin arms; 3 sets/week is a maintenance dose (pressing adds more)
why.forearms: thin arms; deadlifts and rows already load the grip
why.obliques: slim waist; training obliques hard thickens the waist
why.upperAbs: slim waist with the belly kept soft; basic trunk strength only
why.lowerAbs: slim waist with the belly kept soft; basic trunk strength only

hourglass.name: Hourglass
hourglass.summary: Big glutes, capped shoulders and back width over a tight waist; minimal ab and arm work.

why.glutes: the main goal: top of the 8-24 sets/week range, growth keeps rising with volume
why.gluteMed: side of the hip adds width, but it grows less than glute max so moderate volume
why.hamstrings: fills out the back of the thigh; seated curls and hip hinges work well
why.sideDelt: side delts set shoulder width against the hips, they respond to high volume
why.rearDelt: rounds the shoulder from behind and balances the pressing
why.midTraps: upper back thickness and shoulder-width frame
why.lats: lat width gives the upper half of the hourglass
why.adductors: adductor magnus is a big hip extensor that helps fill out the glute-thigh line
why.neck: no need for thickness here, keeps the neck slim
why.forearms: covered by pulling; no extra work wanted
why.tibialis: not part of the look; maintenance only
why.obliques: heavy side-bend work thickens the waist, so only the minimum
why.hipFlexors: no look value; squats and leg raises cover upkeep
why.lowerChest: chest is kept lean, little pressing volume needed
why.serratus: chest-wall detail is minor here; pressing and rows cover it
